verification: Both jobs completed with exit code 0:0 under source_commit. The correlate stage's built-in guard compared its clipped single-direction ICC (replicate 0) against exp-5's signed preflight.json:split_iccs within 1e-4 across all 3 splits and 30 classes; the job did not raise, confirming the reproduced patient/patch sample is identical to exp-5's. The analyze stage's built-in guard compared the single-measure surface's point residual breadth b = gamma_e * ln2 and res_std_neff against exp-5's own analysis.json:surface_parameters within 1e-6; the job did not raise, confirming b=2.9787 and res_std_neff=0.2526 reproduce exp-5 (2.98 and 0.25 as reported). No classifier was retrained; both stages read exp-5's stored predictions and frozen exp-2 feature files only.
run_summary: correlate: per split and class, reproduced exp-5's sampled patient/patch indices, then computed both the single-direction and full-feature covariance-trace ICC on those indices under a shared training-patient cluster bootstrap (2000 replicates, row 0 = unweighted). analyze: clipped and split-averaged the correlations, computed cell effective support per measure, refit the support surface against exp-5's stored bootstrap accuracy distributions (test-patient: correlation fixed at point; training-patient: accuracies fixed at point), and classified the full-feature residual breadth against the +-1pp threshold.
reporting_notes: Full-feature ICC lowers the residual breadth from 2.98 to 2.62 points and improves (does not worsen) the effective-support-only fit (res_std_neff 0.2526 -> 0.2014), yet the full measure's residual breadth interval still lies entirely above 1 point under both test-patient and training-patient resampling: label_test = label_training = breadth_beyond_redundancy, fragile = false.

Paired full-minus-single differences (same bootstrap replicate index for both measures): b differs by -0.359pp (test CI [-0.44, -0.28], training CI [-0.53, -0.30]); res_std_neff differs by -0.051 (test CI [-0.059, -0.030], training CI [-0.090, -0.043]).
